title: Factory repo profile
description: Stack knowledge as data. The implementer/reviewer/qa/release/ops roles read .factory/profile.json at Step 0 and treat it as authoritative for this repo. Role prompts stay byte-identical across every repo in an estate; only this file differs. To change how the factory codes in a repo, edit its profile — not the prompts.

_doc.description: Free-text note for humans. Ignored by the roles.

estate_role.description: One line on where this repo sits among its siblings. The planner and release manager derive cross-repo merge order from these.

stack.description: Languages, frameworks and major libraries, as prose.

branches.description: Branch facts. Implementers cut task branches from the integration branch (`staging`) and base their PRs on it; every change is proved there before it is promoted to `default` (FACTORY.md §6a).

staging.description: This repo's integration branch. The ORG names it in .github/factory-branches.json; set this only when THIS repo's branch is called something else, and it overrides the name (only the name — never whether the step runs). null means the repo has no integration branch yet: with `required: true` in the policy file the Release Manager cuts the org's branch on first use, and only with `required: false` does a null send implementation PRs to `default`.

commands.description: Shell commands, run from the repo root. null means the repo has no such step — roles skip nulls rather than inventing a command.

conventions.description: How code is written here. The implementer follows these after design.md and before CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; the reviewer checks against them.

review_checklist.description: Repo-specific items the reviewer must check on every PR, beyond the generic correctness/security pass.

qa_notes.description: How tests are written and run here — frameworks, mocking boundaries, e2e approach.

gotchas.description: Traps that would otherwise cost an agent a wasted round: pre-existing failures that must not be attributed to the delta, commands that must never be run, invariants that must not be weakened.

reuse_hotspots.description: Paths the reviewer checks before accepting new code, to catch duplication of something that should have been extended.

deploy.description: Post-merge verification. The release manager runs health_checks after each merge; the ops monitor runs them again during soak.

health_checks.description: Concrete, runnable checks — URLs to curl, commands to execute. Not descriptions of checks.

notes.description: Deploy failure modes that must halt a release train.

test_data.description: How one epic's system test data sets get into a running environment and out again (FACTORY.md §4b). Both commands take the epic's data directory (openspec/changes/<epic>-<slug>/system-tests/data) as their last argument. The Test Planner names them in test-data.md, the Release Manager runs load after the staging (or preview) deploy and unload after promotion. Absent means the repo has no loader yet: the first epic with system tests builds one and adds this block.

load.description: Shell command, run from the repo root, that loads every record file in the given directory into the target environment. Idempotent: loading twice must not duplicate.

unload.description: Shell command that removes exactly what load put in.

format.description: The record file format the loader reads — what the Test Planner writes under system-tests/data/. Default json.

notes.description: How the commands find their target environment (an env var, a flag), and anything a tester must do by hand after a load.
